questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
questions.problem: How many made-up $3$-letter words can be made using only $5$ vowels, where each vowel cannot appear in the word more than once?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $5$ vowels, so $n=5.$ We want to select $3$ of those vowels to make-up a $3$-letter word, so we have $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the number of different made-up words is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{P}_{3} & =\frac{5!}{(5-3)!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =5\cdot 4\cdot 3 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: How many made-up $4$-letter words can be made using $21$ consonants, where each consonant cannot appear in the word more than once?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $21$ consonants, so $n=21.$ We want to select $4$ of those consonants to make-up a $4$-letter word, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different made-up words is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{21}{P}_{4} & =\frac{21!}{(21-4)!} \\  & =\frac{21!}{17!} \\  & =\frac{21\cdot 20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot \cancel{17!}}{\cancel{17!}} \\  & =21\cdot 20\cdot 19\cdot 18 \\  & =143\,640.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Permutation Given Using Alternate Notation
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r}$ is given by

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\,.
$$

$P(6,3)$ means the same thing as ${}_{6}{P}_{3}.$ Using the usual formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6,3) & =\frac{6!}{(6-3)!} \\  & =\frac{6!}{3!} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}}{\cancel{3!}} \\  & =6\cdot 5\cdot 4 \\  & =120.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
questions.problem: How many $3$-letter words (legitimate or made-up) can be made using the letters of the word DOCUMENTARY, where each letter cannot appear in the word more than once?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $11$ different letters in the word DOCUMENTARY, so $n=11.$ We want to select $3$ of those letters to make-up a $3$-letter word, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different made-up words is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{11}{P}_{3} & =\frac{11!}{(11-3)!} \\  & =\frac{11!}{8!} \\  & =\frac{11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot \cancel{8!}}{\cancel{8!}} \\  & =11\cdot 10\cdot 9 \\  & =990.\end{aligned}
$$
